# Draft:Roblox Ninja Warrior

Roblox Ninja Warrior is a YouTube sports entertainment reality television show similar to SASUKE and American Ninja Warrior, airing since 2013, in which a varying amount competitors attempt to complete a varying amount-stage obstacle course.
History
In 2013 a man named FluffyTailz2011 made a show like ANW called Roblox Ninja Warrior on January 1st of 2013 which ran for 16 tournaments but it was so famous that many more people made them like BubbaAce37 with Ninja Warrior of Roblox For 22 tournaments and 3 rising tournaments Nicecat9250 (now Ekardus) With Ninja Roblox Warrior which ran for 14 tournaments before being renamed to Ninja Bloxian Warrior for 3 tournaments and BraverCoolio02 (now MisterrrCoolio) with Ninja Coolio Warrior which ran for 25 tournaments before being canceled and for the next 12 years over thousands maybe even millions have tried hundreds and maybe thousands of competitions to achieve KANZENSEIHA
Format
Roblox Ninja Warrior consists of three to five stages of increasing difficulty; competitors must complete a stage to advance.
The object is to hit the buzzer at the end of each course before the allotted time expires. If a competitor goes out of bounds, runs out of time or comes into contact with the water in any of the pits below the course, they are disqualified from the competition.
First stage
The First Stage primarily tests one's speed. Typically, around 80 of the 100 original entrants are eliminated in this stage. However, in competition’s like SASUKE Starhammer 5, Joke SASUKE 5, and JISUKE 5 have an insane amount of the competitors make it past the First Stage with SASUKE Starhammer having 42/85 or 48.23% clear, Joke SASUKE 5 having 13/20 or 65% clear, JISUKE 5 having 21/25 or 84% clear (but it did have the exact same course for the third tournament in a row so it’s fair).
But on the opposite spectrum some have a very scarce amount of clears like SASUKE Nusuntara, Retro SASUKE 2, and Joke SASUKE 3 which basically had no clears with SASUKE Nusuntara having 1/25 or 4% clear, Retro SASUKE 2 having 1/70 or 1.42% clear, and Joke SASUKE 3 insanely having 0/10 or 0% clear
But on extremely few occasions some competitions had every competitor clear like Joke SASUKE 4 having all 10 clear.
Second stage
Those with enough skill to complete Stage One then take on an even more grueling set of obstacles in Stage Two. Hundreds to thousands of competitors have reached the Second Stage as of 2025. Like Stage One, the obstacles alter throughout the competitions. The obstacles determine the time limit, and it is usually between 45 and 120 seconds.
On average, 10 to 25 competitors attempt the Second Stage on each competition. But some has had many clears like Rising Ninja Warrior 4, And JISUKE 2 & 5. With Rising Ninja Warrior 4 having 9/24 or 37.5% clear, JISUKE 5 with 12/21 or 57.14% clear, and JISUKE 2 having 9/12 or 75% clears,
But on the opposite spectrum some have a very scarce amount of clears like Alpha Ninja Warrior 1, Marks Mini 3, and Alpha Ninja Warrior 2 which actually had no clears
But on really extremely few occasions some competitions had every competitor clear like Cyrus SASUKE 23 which had all 6 clear.
Third stage
The Third Stage has no time limit. Contestants are allowed approximately an unlimited amount of seconds of rest between obstacles (which people like ConductiveArrow and Purfugi abuse it so much). While the first two stages focus on speed and agility, this course almost exclusively tests one's upper body strength and stamina.
Out of thousands to millions total competitors and hundreds to thousands Second Stage competitors, hundreds to thousands have attempted the Third Stage. The Third Stage is so grueling that, on average, someone passes it only every other competition. Hundreds of individuals have ever passed it, and only tens have passed it more than once, namely Cyrus08uk, JanterJemote, Bowsypai, ConductiveArrow, Flawduhjit, Andrastical, and Purfugi for some examples. The record for most Third Stage clears in a tournament is 8 in Tri Minh Warrior 2, achieved in the 2nd tournament.
Final stage
To date, the Final Stage has several forms. Each of these share a single, common goal: reach and hit the button at the top before time expires. If the competitor does not reach the top platform in time, the rope is cut and the competitor falls or keep climbing to see if there the fastest. kanzenseiha translated roughly as "complete domination", literally as "complete victory", and rendered on Ninja Warrior as "total victory". The Final Stage's time limit is between 30 and 45 seconds.
